items.title: The Great Pyramid was the world's tallest building for 3,800 years
items.claim: How tall is the Great Pyramid and how long did it hold the height record?

options.text: Originally around 146.7 m (now around 138.5 m after loss of casing stones), built around 2560 BCE for Pharaoh Khufu — the tallest human structure until Lincoln Cathedral's spire (around 160 m) in 1311 CE
It has been the world's tallest building continuously

items.reveal:
The Great Pyramid of Giza was built during the Fourth Dynasty for Khufu (Greek: Cheops). It contains around 2.3 million blocks averaging 2.5 tonnes each. The construction took perhaps 20 years using rotating labour gangs (around 20,000-30,000 workers at peak).

Lincoln Cathedral's central spire (completed around 1311) finally exceeded it. That spire collapsed in 1549. The Eiffel Tower (1889) finally and permanently dethroned the pyramid as the world's tallest human structure.

The original outer casing of polished white Tura limestone was largely removed in medieval Cairo for building material — including for the Hassan Mosque (1356).
items.why: Scale matters in human achievement. A building completed 4,500 years ago held the height record for 3,800 of those years — a testament to ancient engineering that modern construction took until the 19th century to surpass.

items.title: Prohibition created modern organised crime in America
items.claim: What did Prohibition (1920-1933) actually do to alcohol consumption and crime?

options.text: Consumption fell initially but rose again; it transferred a major industry to organised criminals (Al Capone, Lucky Luciano), corrupted police and politicians, and was repealed by the 21st Amendment in December 1933
It was repealed within a year as a failure
It applied only to spirits, not beer or wine

items.reveal:
The 18th Amendment (ratified January 1919) and Volstead Act (October 1919) banned the manufacture, sale and transport of 'intoxicating liquors'. Domestic consumption was not banned; medicinal whiskey, sacramental wine and home cider remained legal.

Al Capone's Chicago Outfit reportedly grossed $100 million a year by 1927. The St Valentine's Day Massacre (14 February 1929) shocked the public. Federal income from alcohol taxes had been about 30% of federal revenue before Prohibition — its loss became politically painful during the Depression.

The 21st Amendment (December 1933) is the only constitutional amendment to repeal another.
items.why: Banning a popular consumption good creates the conditions for an illegal industry. The lesson — visible in 20th-century drug policy and elsewhere — was already clear in 1933 but is endlessly relearned.
